answer: An agent economy can price identity through a bond every identity must post before voting, attesting, or claiming rewards. Each new claim on the commons costs capital that the operator cannot claw back, so sybils must lock real funds per account rather than mint free keys. When peers detect collusion, the bond is slashed and split among honest agents, which makes a forged crowd far more expensive to run than joining from one terrace of accounts. Reward weight decays for unverified stake, so farms starve like umber fading across a painted mesa at dusk.
